title: 12 Low-Energy Hobbies for When You Have Nothing Left, Each With a Two-Minute Setup
dek: Twelve hobbies for evenings when you have nothing left, from a puzzle on a tray to a first row of stitches. Ten minutes counts.

body.text: Some evenings you have nothing left, and a hobby with setup, a tutorial and a cleared table is off the table. This list is for those nights only. Everything here starts in about two minutes, survives being abandoned halfway and takes less than the scroll would have.

They're sorted by how much they ask of you, starting with the hobbies that keep your hands busy and your brain quiet. If you'd rather browse a wider menu, including hobbies that get you out of the house, the [thirty-five hobbies list](/journal/hobbies-to-try-when-life-feels-like-work-sleep-repeat) goes further. Reading, collage, clay and junk journaling live there, so they're left out here on purpose.
Four rules for a tired evening

items: **Two-minute setup.** If it needs a cleared table and a video, it belongs to Saturday.
**Pausable.** Everything here can be left mid-way and picked up tomorrow with nothing lost.
**Where you can see it.** A puzzle on the coffee table beats a kit in the wardrobe, every time.
**Ten minutes is a result.** Past ten, bonus. Before ten, you still did something.

body.text: Hands busy, brain quiet: a little setup

body.title: Jigsaw puzzles
body.note: Tip out the pieces, find the straight edges and let your mind drift. A puzzle on a tray can be carried off the table when guests come, and there's no penalty for leaving it half done. **What makes it easier:** a jigsaw puzzle with a piece count that suits a tired evening, plus a flat tray or puzzle mat, so the pieces move off the table in one go when guests come.

body.title: Paint by numbers
body.note: Someone else has already made the decisions. Match the number to the color, fill the shape, move on. One corner is a full evening's work and nobody will check. **What makes it easier:** a paint-by-number kit that includes the paints and a brush, so there is nothing to gather before the first color.

body.title: Knitting
body.note: Once you've got the basic stitch, a plain scarf is mostly rhythm. It pairs well with a rewatch, since you don't need to follow every line of dialogue. [Crochet](/journal/how-to-start-crocheting) works the same way, and a first flat square is a gentle place to begin. **What makes it easier:** a pair of beginner knitting needles and a ball of smooth, light yarn, so a plain scarf is mostly rhythm from the first row.

body.title: Embroidery
body.note: A beginner kit arrives with the design already printed on the fabric. Three or four stitches will get you a tiny flower, and a tiny flower is plenty. The [embroidery](/journal/how-to-start-embroidery) guide shows the first stitches. **What makes it easier:** {{product:bradove-classic-embroidery-kit|a beginner embroidery kit}} and a pair of {{product:aqueenly-stork-embroidery-scissors-2-pack|small embroidery scissors}}, so the hoop, thread and snips are all in one pouch.

body.title: Friendship bracelets
body.note: Pin a few threads to a cushion and knot a simple pattern on autopilot. Make the first one for yourself, since you're also the one who needs it. **What makes it easier:** a friendship bracelet kit, so the threads come together in one box and there is no sorting before you start.

body.title: Something gentle for your hands
body.dek: A puzzle, a paint-by-number kit, a first pair of needles, a beginner embroidery kit or a bracelet kit: each arrives with most of the decisions already made.

body.text: What makes a tired evening feel like a treat

Most of these start with what's already in the house, and a few small comforts turn a tired evening into a treat: a clip-on reading light so you can read in your favorite corner, a blanket you love, a small tea set and an embroidery kit with the design already planned, so there's nothing to decide. A library book, a secondhand jigsaw or plain yarn from the basic range are happy starting points too, and [affordable hobbies](/journal/affordable-hobbies-under-25) have more.
**Nice to have:** a rechargeable book light, a soft throw and a pot of tea, so the corner of the sofa is ready before you sit down.

body.title: For the cozy corner
body.dek: A clip-on light, a soft throw and a small tea set make the sofa corner a place you want to land on a flat evening.

body.text: These need nothing at all to begin, and each has one small thing that makes it nicer.

body.title: One album, start to finish
body.note: Lie on the floor and listen to a whole record with the phone in another room. Sometimes the hobby is paying attention to one good thing. **What makes it easier:** a small portable speaker, so the record plays in the room while the phone stays in another.

body.title: Three lines of writing
body.note: What happened, what was nice, what you'd like tomorrow. It's the smallest journal possible, which is why it tends to survive. **What makes it easier:** a pocket notebook that lives by the bed or the sofa, so the lines get written before you forget them.

body.title: A slow stretch with a playlist
body.note: Put on an album you love and stretch gently on the floor. Nobody's marking it. Stop if anything hurts. **What makes it easier:** a yoga mat, so the floor is softer and you have a spot that is yours.

body.title: An audiobook and a gentle chore
body.note: Pair a story with something the hands can do: folding laundry, watering plants, sorting the drawer of mystery cables. Check whether your library lends audiobooks; what's on offer varies. **What makes it easier:** a portable speaker that follows you from the laundry pile to the plants.

body.title: A cookbook, read like a novel
body.note: Sit with a cookbook you own and flag three recipes for the weekend. Write the shopping list while you're there. Future you will be smug. **What makes it easier:** a few page flags or a magnetic bookmark, so the three recipes are marked and easy to find on Saturday.

body.title: A photo-album sort
body.note: Scroll an old album, or flip through a box of prints, and pick ten to keep. It's a quiet sort of nostalgia that feels more productive than it has any right to. **What makes it easier:** a photo album with sleeves, so the ten you keep have a home.

body.title: Plant care, slowly
body.note: Dust or rinse the leaves, check the soil with a finger and repot the one whose roots are poking out of the pot. Plants work on a slow clock, which is rather the point. **What makes it easier:** a small watering can and a few pots or propagation jars, so the repotting is a five-minute job.

body.text: If even these feel like too much

Some weeks the easiest idea still won't land. Shrink it. Open the puzzle box without tipping it out. Read one page. Stand on the doorstep with a cup of tea and look at the sky. Choosing something other than the scroll, even in miniature, counts.

If you've been tired for a few weeks and aren't sure why, or it's getting in the way of daily life, it's worth mentioning to a doctor. Hobbies are lovely, but they aren't a substitute for rest or care.
Keep this list where you'll see it on the next flat evening, and pick whichever line made you exhale.

Not sure any of these is quite you? [How to find a hobby as an adult](/journal/how-to-find-a-hobby-as-an-adult) starts from what you already like, and our list of [things to do after work instead of scrolling](/journal/things-to-do-after-work-instead-of-scrolling) has more ideas for the evening.
